items.review_rationale: Read the full cocone and unique mediating map property: F:I→C is a diagram, the maps F(i)→Q are compatible, and every other cocone factors uniquely through Q. Not an ordinary limit with arrows reversed.

references.phrase: cocone morphisms F(i)→Q compatible with the diagram
references.context: Category theory: cocone from a diagram F to a constant object Q

references.phrase: unique factorization of each other cocone
references.context: Category theory: universal initial property among cocones from a fixed diagram

references.disposition: Quantification is over all compatible cocones, not merely all individual maps from one F(i).

items.review_rationale: Read the whole universal cone description, including arrows L→F(i) and unique factorization of every other compatible cone through L. Distinguished direction of cone legs from the colimit cocone.

references.phrase: cone arrows L→F(i) compatible with all arrows of I
references.context: Category theory: compatible cone from an object L to all members of diagram F

references.phrase: unique factorization of every compatible cone through L
references.context: Category theory: terminal universal property in the cone category of a diagram

references.phrase: compatible with every arrow of I
references.disposition: Compatibility of cone legs is part of the object definition and does not require all transition arrows invertible.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed coproduct as colimit of discrete indexed diagram, with injections X_i→Q and the universal outgoing maps property, not as categorical product or mere set disjoint union in all categories.

references.phrase: family of objects X_i in category C

references.context: Category theory: injections from each family object to a coproduct object with unique induced map out

references.disposition: A universal map out of the coproduct is specified; do not reverse it to product projections.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed product as a limit of a discrete indexed diagram, with projections Q→X_i and universal maps into Q. Not necessarily a set Cartesian product or coproduct injections.

references.phrase: objects X_i in a category C

references.context: Category theory: maps from product object to all family objects with unique induced map into product

references.disposition: Universal maps into the product follow projections, not coproduct injections.

items.review_rationale: Read the commutative-ring Jacobson radical as intersection of every maximal ideal of R. Kept maximal ideals distinct from the nilradical or radical ideals, and interpreted intersection set-theoretically.

references.context: Set theory and ring theory: intersection of a family of ideal subsets in a ring

references.disposition: The intersection is over all maximal proper ideals, not all prime ideals and not a single chosen ideal.

items.review_rationale: Read the elementwise Jacobson radical unit test: for every y∈R, 1−xy is invertible. This characterization is distinct from just requiring x itself to be a nonunit, and depends on the unital commutative-ring convention.

references.phrase: for every y∈R, 1−xy is a unit
references.disposition: The universal quantifier on y is essential; testing only y=1 or demanding x be noninvertible would be incorrect.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed both finite-generator and surjection-from-finite-free-module formulations, where n is finite but arbitrary and no presentation relations are required. Distinguishes finite generation from finite presentation and finite cardinality.

references.context: Module theory: module generated by a finite set of elements as all their R-linear combinations
Module theory: surjective R-linear map from finite rank free R-module to M
Module theory: finite direct sum of n copies of R, viewed as free module of rank n

references.disposition: The generator count is finite but does not imply the module has finitely many elements.

items.review_rationale: Read the filtered-colimit Hom characterization for every filtered diagram of modules, retaining the direction and bijectivity of the canonical comparison. A colimit commuting with internal Hom in this sense captures finite presentation, not mere finite generation.

references.context: Module and category theory: map comparing filtered colimit of Hom modules to Hom into filtered colimit

references.disposition: The comparison must be a bijection for all filtered diagrams; this does not follow merely from choosing a single finite generation set.
